title: Shortbread
subtitle: Scottish butter shortbread biscuits
excerpt: Three ingredients: butter, flour, and caster sugar. The ratio is two parts flour to one part butter to half a part sugar. Baked until just pale gold, crumbly and rich. A classic Scottish biscuit.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shortbread is a traditional Scottish biscuit with origins in the 12th century. The classic Petticoat Tails shape, a large round scored into triangular wedges, dates to the 16th century. The three-ingredient formula is 2:1:0.5, flour to butter to sugar. Good butter makes a significant difference. The biscuit should be pale gold, not brown, and will be soft when it comes from the oven, firming as it cools.

content.text: The butter must be soft enough to cream but not melted. Do not over-work the dough: mix only until it comes together, then chill. The biscuits are done when they are pale gold, not brown. They will feel soft when they come out of the oven and harden as they cool.
Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and smooth. Add the flour and salt. Mix until the dough comes together. It will be crumbly at first but should form a dough when pressed.
Shape into a disc, wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3.
Roll out on a lightly floured surface to 1 cm thick. Cut into fingers or rounds and arrange on lined baking trays. Prick each biscuit several times with a fork.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until pale gold. They should not colour at the edges. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.
